memberdef.name: d2f_dT2

briefdescription.para: Computes the second derivative of a function that maps a tensor to a scalar.

parameterdescription.para: dimension of the input tensor (dim x dim)
function mapping a (dim x dim) tensor to a scalar
input tensor at which the derivative is evaluated

simplesect.para: tuple of function value, first derivative and second derivative of F with respect to T first derivative has shape (dim, dim) second derivative has shape (dim, dim, dim, dim)
The implementation is currently limited to second rank (dim x dim) tensors

parameterdescription.para: if true, T is assumed to be symmetric, e.g. the right Cauchy-Green tensor, and F is assumed to be a transpose-invariant scalar function of T (as is the case for any scalar function built from tensor invariants). This reduces the number of outer-pair seed directions from dim^2 to dim*(dim+1)/2 a ~1.5x reduction for dim=3, approaching (but never reaching) a 2x reduction as dim grows by exploiting the identity $ \partial^2 F / \partial T_{ij}\partial T_{kl} = \partial^2 F/\partial T_{ji}\partial T_{lk} $, which holds at a symmetric T for such functions (note: this mirrors both index pairs simultaneously; mirroring either pair independently is in general NOT valid)

memberdef.argsstring: (const tensor_and_scalar_to_scalar_function_type< dim > &F, const Fastor::Tensor< double, dim, dim > &T, const double scalar, bool isSymmetric=false)
memberdef.name: d2f_dTensor_dScalar

briefdescription.para: Computes the mixed second derivative of a function that maps a tensor and a scalar to a scalar.

parameterdescription.para: dimension of the input tensor (dim x dim)
function mapping a (dim x dim) tensor and a scalar to a scalar
input tensor at which the derivative is evaluated
input scalar at which the derivative is evaluated

simplesect.para: mixed second derivative of F with respect to T and the scalar, has shape (dim, dim)
The implementation is currently limited to second rank (dim x dim) tensors

parameterdescription.para: if true, T (and thus the resulting derivative) is assumed to be symmetric, e.g. the right Cauchy-Green tensor. Only the dim*(dim+1)/2 upper-triangle entries of T are seeded, and the result is mirrored to the lower triangle, instead of all dim^2 entries a ~1.5x reduction in function evaluations for dim=3; the fraction of evaluations needed, (dim+1)/(2*dim), approaches but never reaches 1/2 as dim grows, so this never fully halves the evaluation count
